goals.title: Feed more people, more reliably
goals.detail: By Sep 30, 2029, serve 4,000 meals a year (plated meals, food bags and community kitchen portions), counted per service in the Hub, by running all 26 scheduled Montreal services and monthly Toronto services.
goals.why: The meal is the mission. FY26 completed 17 Montreal services and cancelled 6.

paths.body: Count meals at every service in the Hub from Oct 2026.
A backup lead and minimum crew for every Sunday service.
Grow the community kitchen model piloted with DESTA on 23 Aug 2026.

A monthly Toronto cadence with shelter partners and TYFPC (Cook & Support partnership, Oct 2026 to Jul 2027, with a TMU Cook & Share in Jan 2027), building toward a Toronto food bank with Daily Bread (a 2 to 3 year aim in the 2026 plan).

milestones.body: 26 Montreal services, none cancelled for staffing
Toronto food bank open with Daily Bread
Weekly Montreal only if the FY29 gate is met

goals.title: Go beyond the meal
goals.detail: By Sep 30, 2029, every service offers hygiene kits, 1 in 4 services has a referral partner on site (including housing organizations), and beneficiaries give feedback twice a year.
goals.why: "Meals and essential support" is in the mission; reintegration is the stated north star. We distributed 280 hygiene products in 2025.
goals.target_fy29: 100% hygiene kits; referral partner at 1 in 4
goals.target_fy31: 5 beneficiaries in a paid pathways pilot

paths.body: Source kits through partners.

Invite referral partners from our 73 active partners, with housing organizations a priority so we can connect people to housing support, and publish the resource guide (print and digital) from the June 2026 Program Portfolio.
Complete the beneficiary feedback project (0 of 2 tasks done).

milestones.body: 2 referral partners committed, at least 1 a housing organization
Grant-funded pathways pilot: 5 beneficiaries in paid roles at $16.25/hr

goals.title: Grow a team that stays
goals.detail: By Sep 30, 2029, 35% of each year's volunteers serve again the next year, 150 unique volunteers serve a year, and no leader averages more than 6 hours a week.
goals.why: Retention fell from 17% (FY25) to 13% (FY26). In FY26, 12 of 42 applicants went on to serve.

paths.body: Follow up with every first-time volunteer within 7 days.
The ambassador tier and role descriptions recommended by 180DC.
Decide the open volunteer recognition budget.

goals.title: Build money that lasts
goals.detail: By Sep 30, 2029, reach $60,000 in annual revenue with no single source above 40%, fund two part-time paid roles, hold 3 months of expenses in reserve, and raise at least $20,000 a year from grants.
goals.why: Revenue has stayed between $10,553 and $15,347 since FY23, all recorded as donations. Three months of the FY26 budget ($19,240 in expenses) is $4,810.

owners.name: Ian
owners.focus: Donor marketing and the Ad Grant

paths.body: Grants: Centraide (pending); joint applications with DESTA, and with TYFPC to Maytree (about $5,000).
Donor program: the donor team (Alexis, Danielle) launches monthly giving in FY27, with QR codes at services (decided June 2026).
Corporate Supporter Circle: 2 to 6 companies at $200 to $500 a quarter.
Google Ad Grant: $10,000 a month, unused today.

Flagship events: Flag Football, Rally Paper and the holiday drive grow into flagship events, plus one new signature event by FY28 (the 2027 sports tournament in the events calendar). Every event gets a named lead; none of the 22 planned FY27 events has one today.

Paid roles: funded by grants and wage subsidies, never general donations. Canada Summer Jobs first (MCC estimated about $15,000 a year for two summer roles), then the Trillium ask (up to $100,000, 60% for a full-time Toronto role) for a year-round role.

milestones.body: First paid roles: 2 Canada Summer Jobs positions for summer 2027 (window may reopen Nov 2026)
A multi-year funder covering a paid program lead

goals.title: Run on systems, not heroes
goals.detail: By Sep 30, 2029, every leadership role has a written description, a 3 to 6 hour expectation and a trained backup; 7 board seats are filled with 4 committees meeting quarterly; and the Hub is the single system of record.
goals.why: Many roles turn over each school year, the board has an open HR seat, and the organization is moving from founder-led to board-led.
goals.measure: Leadership roles with a written role and trained backup
goals.target_fy31: Toronto runs as a self-led chapter

paths.body: Complete the executive transition.
A yearly handover cycle timed to the school year.
Retire Keela into the Hub CRM.
Use MCC's chapter model for Toronto.

milestones.body: Toronto self-led with its own fundraising
Decide on a new city (MCC recommended Calgary), only if the FY29 gate is met

plan.mission: Welfare Avenue is a youth-powered non-profit dedicated to fighting food insecurity and poverty through direct community action. We deliver meals and essential support directly to people where they are.
plan.mission_note: The mission adopted in July 2026. Every goal serves it.
plan.window: Five goals for FY27 to FY29 (Oct 1, 2026 to Sep 30, 2029), with a gated view to FY31.
plan.why_reset: At the July 2026 mid-year check, program impact was behind and the financial cushion had not started. This plan keeps the ambition and adds what was missing: a baseline, owners, yearly milestones, and a named engine (donor team, flagship events, grants, paid roles) behind every number. Targets start from measured baselines. All targets are proposals for board approval.
plan.long_range: Leadership's long-range target (Oct 2025) is $5 million in revenue and 1 million meals within 10 years, in five cities. This plan is the first five years toward it.
plan.rule: One owner, one Hub measure, and no leader asked to exceed 6 hours a week.

roadmap.title: Three years to prove it, then grow through the FY29 gate
roadmap.gate_rule: FY30 and FY31 targets apply only if all four gate criteria are met in October 2029; otherwise FY29 targets carry forward.

cadence: Quarterly board meetings (Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct): a one-page scorecard, one line per goal.
Every board meeting: the standing strategy block (board item 18).
Each October: a year-end strategy session (board item 13) that resets next year's milestones.
